content:
## 题目
Find a basis \(\{p(x),q(x)\}\) for the vector space  
\[
\{f(x)\in \mathbb P_3[x] \mid f'(5)=f(1)\},
\]
where \(\mathbb P_3[x]\) is the vector space of polynomials in \(x\) with degree less than \(3\).

## 解法
Over the real numbers, this solution uses the matrix method with coordinates relative to the standard basis \(B=\{1,x,x^2\}\).

Write a general polynomial as
\[
f(x)=a+bx+cx^2.
\]
Then
\[
[f]_B=\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\\c\end{pmatrix}.
\]
The condition is
\[
f'(5)=f(1).
\]
Compute:
\[
f'(x)=b+2cx,
\]
so
\[
f'(5)=b+10c,
\]
and
\[
f(1)=a+b+c.
\]
Thus
\[
f'(5)-f(1)=(b+10c)-(a+b+c)=-a+9c.
\]
The condition \(f'(5)=f(1)\) becomes
\[
-a+9c=0.
\]
In matrix form, the subspace is the nullspace of
\[
A=\begin{bmatrix}-1&0&9\end{bmatrix}.
\]
The augmented matrix is already reduced:
\[
\begin{bmatrix}
-1&0&9&|&0
\end{bmatrix}.
\]
So
\[
a=9c.
\]
Hence the coordinate vectors in the nullspace are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\\c\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}9c\\b\\c\end{pmatrix}
=
b\begin{pmatrix}0\\1\\0\end{pmatrix}
+
c\begin{pmatrix}9\\0\\1\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Therefore, a coordinate basis is
\[
(0,1,0)^T,\qquad (9,0,1)^T.
\]
Converting back to polynomials:
\[
(0,1,0)^T \leftrightarrow x,
\]
and
\[
(9,0,1)^T \leftrightarrow 9+x^2.
\]
Thus
\[
p(x)=x,\qquad q(x)=x^2+9.
\]

## 约定
- Standard basis \(B=\{1,x,x^2\}\), coefficient order \((a,b,c)\).
- Free variables chosen as \(b\) and \(c\).
- Basis order \(p(x)=x\), \(q(x)=x^2+9\).

来源：自行选取

## 答案
\[
p(x)=x,\qquad q(x)=x^2+9.
\]

## 可核对结论
- 类型：基（basis）
- 结论：x | x^2+9
- 约定：\(B=(1,x,x^2)\); \(p=x,\ q=x^2+9\)
- 约定来源：自行选取

## 检验
For \(p(x)=x\):
\[
p'(5)=1=p(1).
\]
For \(q(x)=x^2+9\):
\[
q'(x)=2x,\qquad q'(5)=10,
\]
and
\[
q(1)=1+9=10.
\]
Thus both polynomials satisfy the condition. Their coordinate vectors \((0,1,0)^T\) and \((9,0,1)^T\) are linearly independent. The matrix \(A\) has rank \(1\), so its nullspace has dimension \(3-1=2\), matching the two basis vectors.
